# Azure AI Gateway Labs

> Hands-on labs to govern every model, tool, and agent from one gateway.

Hands-on labs for the AI Gateway tier of Azure API Management. Each lab has portal, Azure CLI, REST, Bicep, or code tracks.

Product docs: https://ai.gateway.azure.com/docs
Portal: https://ai.gateway.azure.com
Source: https://github.com/Azure/ai-gateway/tree/main/labs

## Labs

- [00 How Azure AI Gateway works](https://azure.github.io/ai-gateway/labs/00-how-ai-gateway-works/index.md): A 20-minute visual tour of the AI Gateway tier of Azure API Management. Follow one request through the gateway, meet models, aliases, MCP servers, policies, and identities, and pick the learning path that fits your role.
- [01 Provision your AI Gateway](https://azure.github.io/ai-gateway/labs/01-provision-gateway/index.md): Create the shared AI Gateway that your apps and agents will call, from the AI Gateway portal, the Azure CLI, or Bicep, then take a guided tour of the portal.
- [02 Publish a Foundry model and make your first call](https://azure.github.io/ai-gateway/labs/02-first-model-call/index.md): Publish a Microsoft Foundry model deployment through your gateway with its managed identity, create a runtime API key, try the model in the Discover playground, and call it from curl, PowerShell, Python, TypeScript, and C#.
- [03 Publish models from any provider behind stable aliases](https://azure.github.io/ai-gateway/labs/03-multi-provider-aliases/index.md): Connect Anthropic or another non-Azure provider with a credential that stays in the gateway, publish its models behind callable aliases, call Claude with the native Messages API, and retarget an alias to a different backend model without changing a single client.
- [04 Federate MCP tools behind one endpoint](https://azure.github.io/ai-gateway/labs/04-federate-mcp-tools/index.md): Register a remote MCP server in AI Gateway, add a second backend under its own namespace, and connect curl, VS Code, and Python to one governed MCP endpoint.
- [05 Control which tools agents can call](https://azure.github.io/ai-gateway/labs/05-mcp-tool-controls/index.md): Publish only approved MCP tools with name patterns, block risky tools, take a whole MCP server offline, and cap tool traffic per caller with a request rate limit.
- [06 Throttle tokens per caller with token limits](https://azure.github.io/ai-gateway/labs/06-token-limits/index.md): Cap how many tokens each app, agent, or user can consume per minute, hour, or day, and watch the gateway answer with 429 and Retry-After before your backend capacity runs out.
- [07 Enforce cost budgets with per-caller overrides](https://azure.github.io/ai-gateway/labs/07-cost-budgets/index.md): Give every app, agent, and user a dollar budget per hour, day, or month, raise or lower it for specific API keys and Microsoft Entra identities, and watch the gateway answer 403 LlmCostQuotaExceeded once a caller's estimated spend runs out.
- [08 Screen prompts and responses with content safety](https://azure.github.io/ai-gateway/labs/08-content-safety/index.md): Add a content safety policy that screens prompts, tool inputs, and responses for hate, self-harm, sexual, and violent content, tune each category's threshold, and see how blocked calls return 400.
- [09 Set gateway-wide policy baselines](https://azure.github.io/ai-gateway/labs/09-gateway-baselines/index.md): Apply a baseline of token limit, request rate limit, content safety, and IP filter policies at Gateway scope so every model and MCP server, including the ones you add later, starts with the same guardrails, then layer stricter asset policies on top.
- [10 Issue and rotate runtime API keys](https://azure.github.io/ai-gateway/labs/10-api-keys/index.md): Give every app its own runtime API key, keep the value out of your code, rotate it without downtime with the primary and secondary values, revoke a leaked key, and see usage and cost per key in Monitoring.
- [11 Go keyless with Microsoft Entra ID and RBAC](https://azure.github.io/ai-gateway/labs/11-entra-rbac/index.md): Replace shared gateway API keys with Microsoft Entra ID tokens. Grant users, groups, apps, and managed identities an AI Gateway data-plane role at the gateway, a model alias, or an MCP server, then call models from the playground, curl, Python, TypeScript, and C# with no secret in code.
- [12 Call backends with managed identities](https://azure.github.io/ai-gateway/labs/12-backend-identity/index.md): Let the gateway reach Microsoft Foundry with a managed identity instead of stored keys. Check the system-assigned identity, then create a user-assigned identity you can share across gateways, grant it Foundry User, attach it, and point a model provider at it from the portal, the Azure CLI, or Bicep.
- [13 Monitor usage, cost, and traces](https://azure.github.io/ai-gateway/labs/13-monitoring/index.md): Send the gateway's OpenTelemetry metrics, logs, and traces to Application Insights, then use the built-in Monitoring dashboard to see usage, estimated cost per model and API key, policy impact, and gateway-aware traces.
- [14 Attribute tokens and cost with OpenTelemetry](https://azure.github.io/ai-gateway/labs/14-otel-chargeback/index.md): Export Microsoft Entra token claims with the gateway's logs, traces, and token metrics, then turn observed tokens into a per-tenant, per-app, and per-key chargeback report with KQL, PromQL, and a small Python script.
- [15 Connect agent frameworks to models and tools](https://azure.github.io/ai-gateway/labs/15-agent-frameworks/index.md): Point Microsoft Agent Framework, the OpenAI Agents SDK, and LangChain with LangGraph at the gateway's OpenAI-compatible model endpoint and its MCP endpoint, so every model and tool call an agent makes passes through gateway policies and shows up in Monitoring.
- [16 Deploy a Foundry hosted agent behind AI Gateway](https://azure.github.io/ai-gateway/labs/16-foundry-hosted-agent/index.md): Deploy your own Microsoft Agent Framework agent to Foundry Hosted Agents with azd. The agent has no model deployment and no direct tool access, so its model calls and its Microsoft Learn MCP calls go through AI Gateway with a dedicated key. Run it locally, invoke it in Foundry, and cap its tokens without changing its code.
- [17 Build on your gateway with coding agents](https://azure.github.io/ai-gateway/labs/17-coding-agent-plugin/index.md): Install the AI Gateway plugin in GitHub Copilot CLI, Claude Code, Cursor, or Gemini CLI, then let your coding agent discover the gateway's models and MCP tools and generate working client code.
- [18 Lock down backend traffic with private networking](https://azure.github.io/ai-gateway/labs/18-private-networking/index.md): Create an AI Gateway with private routing through your virtual network, reach a Foundry backend over a private endpoint with its public access turned off, and learn which inbound options aren't available yet.
- [19 Protect tool calls with Agent 365 threat protection](https://azure.github.io/ai-gateway/labs/19-tool-threat-protection/index.md): Have Microsoft Defender and Microsoft Purview evaluate every tool call on an MCP server, before the tool runs, after it returns, or both, and see how a fail-closed denial reaches the caller.
- [20 Govern MCP servers with Agent 365](https://azure.github.io/ai-gateway/labs/20-agent-365-governance/index.md): Connect Microsoft Agent 365 to your gateways, find their MCP servers in one inventory, block a single tool or a whole server from the Microsoft 365 admin center, and see exactly what agents get back.
- [21 Deploy an enterprise reference architecture](https://azure.github.io/ai-gateway/labs/21-enterprise-reference/index.md): Deploy a production-shaped AI Gateway environment from modular Bicep, with a keyless Foundry backend, models and MCP tools behind RBAC, a key per app, layered policies, and monitoring. Then promote it from dev to prod with a GitHub Actions workflow that signs in with OpenID Connect and smoke-tests every deployment.

## Learning paths

- 30-minute quickstart: 00-how-ai-gateway-works, 01-provision-gateway, 02-first-model-call, 04-federate-mcp-tools
- Platform engineer: 01-provision-gateway, 02-first-model-call, 03-multi-provider-aliases, 04-federate-mcp-tools, 09-gateway-baselines, 12-backend-identity, 18-private-networking, 21-enterprise-reference
- App & agent developer: 02-first-model-call, 03-multi-provider-aliases, 04-federate-mcp-tools, 15-agent-frameworks, 16-foundry-hosted-agent, 17-coding-agent-plugin
- Security & compliance: 10-api-keys, 11-entra-rbac, 08-content-safety, 05-mcp-tool-controls, 09-gateway-baselines, 19-tool-threat-protection, 20-agent-365-governance
- FinOps & operations: 06-token-limits, 07-cost-budgets, 13-monitoring, 14-otel-chargeback
